source.title: Be Kind, Rewrite: Benign Projections via Rewriting Defend Against LLM Data Poisoning Attacks

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning with harmful poisoned data can produce harmful compliance, using backdoor and poison-injection attacks and ASR measures rather than the original fine-tuning setup. It does not test the claim about benign-only fine-tuning or shallow safety representations.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports average ASR over five backdoor attacks for each model and defense; Table 4 reports StrongREJECT ASR for pre-PIA models, PIA fine-tuning without defense, and proactive defenses. The poisoned datasets contain harmful samples, so these results do not test benign-only fine-tuning. Related-work results cited from other papers are not recorded. Runtime and natural-language benchmark results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense paper, but its no-defense PIA results test V1 in a new setting. Four instruct models were fine-tuned with Q-LoRA on 5,000 samples, 2% of them (about 100) harmful. StrongREJECT ASR is reported before and after (Table 4). The backdoor results have no pre-attack reference and measure trigger-conditional compliance. All defense rows compare the authors' method with other mitigations, so they do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that open-book rewriting (OBBR) of training data is the most effective defense against backdoor and poison-injection attacks, cheaper than CLEANGEN or CROW, and does not hurt benchmark performance. They also state that existing intraactive and reactive defenses barely reduce ASR. They add that PIAs drastically degrade safety guardrails, e.g. Llama-3.1-8B going from under 3% to 72% compliance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses five backdoor attack patterns and a poison-injection dataset, fine-tunes instruct checkpoints for five epochs, and evaluates triggered ASR or StrongREJECT compliance. This is not the original benign fine-tuning recipe. The rewriting defenses are data sanitization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR differs by model and defense; OBBR, CBBR, DPR, Paraphrase, CROW, CLEANGEN, Quantize, and Decoding yield different outcomes. The backdoor measure averages five attack patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Backdoor fine-tuning (400 trigger-poisoned plus 400 benign samples) yields 68.7–84.2% non-refusal on triggered prompts, with no pre-attack reference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trigger-conditional backdoor fine-tuning installs harmful compliance in safety-trained models.

record.problems: Table 1 reports averages across five backdoor patterns rather than attack-specific values, and gives no pre-backdoor ASR reference. The PIA experiment has a pre-PIA reference, but reports no uncertainty estimates; compliance is evaluated with a fine-tuned StrongREJECT evaluator. Results establish effects for these poisoning procedures, not benign-only fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported ASR values in Tables 1 and 4 were left out. Non-ASR runtime and natural-language benchmark results were omitted because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Dose-response over number of harmful examples; only one mix (2% of 5,000) is tested; no closed models.
All: no benign-only fine-tuning condition (the LIMA runs report only capability benchmarks, not safety).
All: no prefilling, suffix or decoding bypass.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label is dropped: defense effectiveness is mitigation, not a condition qualifying V1. The Qwen models already comply with 20–27% of requests before PIA, but the rise is still large. ASR is judged by the StrongREJECT fine-tuned Gemma-2B evaluator; no uncertainty is reported. Harmful examples sit inside a 98% benign mix, consistent with V1's 'few hundred' range.

versions.untested_parts: No direct comparison of the same models before and after backdoor fine-tuning is reported in Table 1; the ASR there is averaged across five attacks and requires triggers. PIA results provide pre-PIA comparisons. The study does not establish that refusal is removed almost entirely.
The fine-tuning datasets include explicit harmful poisoned examples; no ordinary or carefully selected benign-only fine-tuning condition is tested.
No per-token KL or response-position distribution comparison.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial-suffix attack, or test that decoding changes bypass safety; decoding is evaluated as a defense against backdoors.
No test of whether safety is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
No test of whether fine-tuning data or objective causes safety shallowness.
No training intended to spread safety across response positions or test of whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: Table 4 directly measures increased harmful compliance after fine-tuning with 100 malicious examples among 5,000 samples.

tranche.reason: The no-defense PIA experiments test V1 in a mixed-data poisoning setting on four newer instruct checkpoints, with pre/post StrongREJECT measurements.

source_check.notes: Backdoor values are averages over five attacks; Base denotes attacked models without defense, not pre-attack checkpoints. Capability checks use separate LIMA fine-tuning experiments and do not establish capability preservation after PIA.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PIA fine-tuning without defense, all four tested instruct models
reader_labels.reason: StrongREJECT ASR rises from the pre-PIA reference to 57.2, 70.9, 76.2, and 72.0, respectively (P-L32-Pre, P-L32-None, P-Q25-15-Pre, P-Q25-15-None, P-Q25-7-Pre, P-Q25-7-None, P-L31-8-Pre, P-L31-8-None). This supports harmful poisoned fine-tuning raising harmful compliance in this setting.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Backdoor fine-tuning and PIA fine-tuning with the tested defenses
reader_labels.reason: The backdoor ASR is conditional on triggers, and rewriting or other defenses changes ASR substantially; PIA defense outcomes also vary. The results do not show refusal removed almost entirely in every tested condition (B-L32-Base through B-L31-8-Decoding; P-L32-OBBR through P-L31-8-Paraphrase).
